target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures relate to cash dividends paid to shareholders. The 2024 disclosure reports $395 million paid in FY2024. The 2025 disclosure reports $834 million paid in FY2025. They share the specific topic of historical cash dividend payments, which is part of the 'Capital Return to Shareholders' section in both years.

Both disclosures discuss the Board of Directors' discretion and determination regarding future cash dividend payments. The 2024 disclosure explicitly states the program is subject to the Board's determination of being in shareholders' best interests. The 2025 disclosure mirrors this language in the same section ('Capital Return to Shareholders'), making nvda_2025_7_D069 a multi-faceted match covering both past payments and future policy, similar to how nvda_2024_7_D078 covered policy while D077 covered payments. To ensure all required IDs are covered and specific links are preserved, D077 and D078 are matched to the same current D069 which contains both aspects, or D078 is matched to D069's policy sentence. Since D069 contains both, it is a valid match for the topic of dividend policy/policy statement present in D078.

comparisons.peer_summary: Liquidity needs primarily stem from working capital, R&D, capital expenditures, dividends, taxes, and payments on $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, with capital expenditures expected to be higher in fiscal 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom identify cash dividends as a component of their liquidity requirements. Broadcom explicitly lists 'cash dividend payments (if and when declared by our Board of Directors)' as a primary source of short-term and long-term liquidity requirements, noting they are declared at the Board's discretion. NVIDIA similarly frames its dividend program as being subject to the Board's continuing determination, aligning with the discretionary nature of the liability Broadcom accounts for in its liquidity planning.

sentences.text: Our cash dividend program and the payment of future cash dividends under that program are subject to our Board of Directors' continuing determination that the dividend program and the declaration of dividends thereunder are in the best interests of our shareholders.

Our short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from: (i) business acquisitions and investments we may make from time to time, (ii) working capital requirements, (iii) research and development and capital expenditure needs, (iv) cash dividend payments (if and when declared by our Board of Directors), (v) interest and principal payments related to our $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, and (vi) payment of income taxes.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company suspended quarterly dividends starting Q4 2024 and is prohibited from paying dividends for two years under its commercial CHIPS Act agreement, with limitations for three years thereafter, citing a focus on critical investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the governance and status of the cash dividend program, though with opposite outcomes. NVIDIA affirms its ongoing dividend program is subject to the Board's continuing determination to act in shareholders' best interests. In contrast, Intel discloses a suspension of its quarterly dividends starting in Q4 2024, prohibited for two years under a CHIPS Act agreement, indicating the Board's determination was that dividends were not currently in the best interest of shareholders due to a focus on critical investments and regulatory constraints. Both highlight the Board's central role in determining dividend policy.

sentences.text: Our cash dividend program and the payment of future cash dividends under that program are subject to our Board of Directors' continuing determination that the dividend program and the declaration of dividends thereunder are in the best interests of our shareholders.
We suspended the declaration of quarterly dividends starting with Q4 2024.
Further, we do not expect to pay dividends until our cash flows improve as we focus on the critical investments needed to execute our business strategy and create long-term value.

comparisons.peer_summary: A quarterly dividend of $0.115 per share was declared on September 25, 2024, payable in October 2024, with future dividends subject to Board discretion based on factors including financial condition, capital requirements, and regulatory constraints.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Micron disclose that their respective cash dividend programs and future payments are subject to the continuing discretion and determination of their Board of Directors. NVIDIA states the program is subject to the Board's determination that it is in the 'best interests of our shareholders,' while Micron explicitly details that the Board's decisions depend on factors such as financial condition, capital requirements, and regulatory constraints. Both disclosures affirm that dividends are not obligatory and remain at the Board's discretion.

sentences.text: Our cash dividend program and the payment of future cash dividends under that program are subject to our Board of Directors' continuing determination that the dividend program and the declaration of dividends thereunder are in the best interests of our shareholders.
The declaration and payment of any future cash dividends are at the discretion and subject to the approval of our Board of Directors.

Our Board of Directors' decisions regarding the amount and payment of dividends will depend on many factors, including, but not limited to, our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, business conditions, debt service obligations, contractual restrictions, industry practice, legal requirements, regulatory constraints, and other factors that our Board of Directors may deem relevant.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company announced a $0.85 per share cash dividend payable in December 2024 to stockholders of record as of early December 2024, intending to continue using dividends to return capital.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Qualcomm discuss their cash dividend programs and the governance criteria for future payments. Qualcomm states its intention to use cash dividends 'subject to capital availability and our view that cash dividends are in the best interests of our stockholders.' NVIDIA similarly states that its cash dividend program is subject to the Board's continuing determination that payments are 'in the best interests of our shareholders.' Both disclosures highlight the discretionary nature of dividends based on shareholder interest, whereas NVIDIA focuses on the Board's authority and Qualcomm on the capital availability and strategic view.
